--- title: "Quickstart" --- We take one district from a measured prevalence to a plotted trajectory. Under-5 prevalence there is 0.45, pyrethroid resistance is 0.30, and the nets in the ground are pyrethroid-only at 0.70 coverage. Transmission is perennial. The campaign replaces those nets with pyrethroid-PBO at the same coverage. ## One scenario A `Scenario` holds one candidate campaign, describing both the setting as it stands and the intervention that switches on at the campaign, with the five fields between `name` and `eir_target` giving the setting, the `py_*` fields the current net mix, and the `*_future` fields the campaign itself. `EirTarget(0.45, "prevalence")` tells `run_scenarios` that 0.45 is a measured prevalence rather than an EIR, so it is inverted into a baseline EIR first. The emulator never sees the prevalence. ::: {#0abf7655 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from estimint import Scenario, EirTarget, run_scenarios pbo = Scenario( name="PBO switch", res_use=0.30, # pyrethroid resistance Q0=0.85, # share of bites taken on humans phi=0.80, # share of bites taken in bed seasonal=0.0, # 0 perennial, 1 strongly seasonal irs=0.0, # current IRS coverage eir_target=EirTarget(0.45, "prevalence"), py_only=0.70, # current nets: pyrethroid-only at 70% coverage itn_future=0.70, # the campaign: same coverage... net_type_future="pyrethroid_pbo", # ...different net ) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## Future coverage must be set explicitly Note that `itn_future=0.70` does not mean "keep the nets you have". Leave it out and both `dn0_future` and `itn_future` are set to zero, which models the nets being **withdrawn** at the campaign rather than continuing. The same holds for `irs_future`, which does not inherit `irs`. Every intervention you want to persist past the campaign must be restated in its `_future` field, even when nothing about it changes. ::: ## Run the scenario `run_scenarios` takes a list of scenarios, one here and hundreds later. It converts each net mix and resistance level to `dn0`, inverts each measured prevalence to a baseline EIR, and calls the emulator. It returns one row per scenario. ::: {#b52a15b6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} results = run_scenarios([pbo]) results.drop(columns=["prevalence", "cases"]).T ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
0
name PBO switch
input_mode prevalence
net py_only
net_future pyrethroid_pbo
dn0_use 0.311
itn_use 0.7
irs_use 0.0
dn0_future 0.48495
itn_future 0.7
irs_future 0.0
routine 0.0
lsm 0.0
seasonal 0.0
eir_baseline 31.960129
mosquito_delta 0.0
eir_final 31.960129
hbr_baseline NaN
hbr_new NaN
prev_y9 0.456028
prev_endline 0.470118
cases_endline 2.412444
``` ::: ::: Each row of that transposed column is one field of the result. `dn0_use` is the lethality of the nets in the ground today, and `dn0_future` the lethality of the PBO nets replacing them. Coverage is unchanged at 0.70. The switch between those two numbers is the whole intervention. `eir_baseline` is the transmission intensity implied by a prevalence of 0.45 in this setting. The units are infectious bites per person per year. `prev_y9` is prevalence at the campaign, `prev_endline` three years after it, and `cases_endline` the clinical case rate there. `hbr_baseline` and `hbr_new` are `NaN`. They are only computed when a prevalence input is paired with a non-zero `mosquito_delta`, and this scenario perturbs nothing about mosquito density. ## The trajectory The two columns dropped from the table, `prevalence` and `cases`, hold the trajectories, each cell a 157-element NumPy array rather than a tidy long table. The elements are 14-day windows starting at day 2190, with the campaign at day 3285. Expressed as years from the campaign, that is three years of baseline against three years of response. ::: {#4e153977 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np prev = results.loc[0, "prevalence"] abs_t = 2190 + 14 * np.arange(len(prev)) # day of each 14-day window years = (abs_t - 3285) / 365 # years from the campaign print(prev.shape, years[0].round(2), years[-1].round(2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (157,) -3.0 2.98 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#60de719b .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4)) ax.plot(years, prev, color="#00d4aa", lw=2) ax.axvline(0, color="#8b93a3", ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.7) ax.set_xlabel("Years from the campaign") ax.set_ylabel("Under-5 prevalence") ax.set_ylim(0, None) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Under-5 prevalence for a switch to pyrethroid-PBO nets at 0.70 coverage, in a setting with resistance 0.30 and a measured prevalence of 0.45. The grey dashed line marks the campaign.](quickstart_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){fig-alt='A green line chart of prevalence against years from the campaign. Prevalence wanders between about 0.29 and 0.50 over the three years before the campaign and reaches 0.46 at it, then drops sharply to about 0.26 a year after the campaign before climbing back to about 0.47 by the end of the third year.'} ::: ::: Prevalence drops sharply once the PBO nets go out. The green line reaches its minimum about a year past the grey dashed campaign line, then climbs back over the remaining two years to finish close to where it started. This is because the insecticide on a net decays across the three years it spends in the field. The endline value on its own understates the campaign. The three years before the campaign are not flat. Nor are they expected to be. `EirTarget` pins prevalence at the campaign, where `prev_y9` comes out at 0.456 against the 0.45 that was measured, and everything to the left of the dashed line is the emulator's own history of the setting under the nets already in place. ## See also The four quantities moving through this scenario are defined in [EIR, HBR, prevalence, and cases](../03-concepts/equilibrium.qmd), and the resistance curves behind `dn0` in [Nets and dn0](../04-estimint/nets-and-dn0.qmd). Every field of `Scenario` is covered in [One call, end to end](../06-scenarios/run-scenarios.qmd), and [Comparing campaigns](../06-scenarios/comparing.qmd) runs five campaigns against each other in this same district. Please see [Coming from R](coming-from-r.qmd) for the pandas idioms behind these tables.
